lines.text: One point inside a rectangle makes four triangles. You know three of their areas.
lines.caption: One point inside a rectangle makes four triangles. You know three of their areas.

lines.text: Can you find the fourth, without knowing where the point is? <short pause> You can!
lines.caption: Can you find the fourth, without knowing where the point is? You can!

lines.text: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this puzzle together.
lines.caption: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this puzzle together.

lines.text: Here's the question. Point P is inside a rectangle, and it's joined to all four corners.
lines.caption: Here's the question. Point P is inside a rectangle, and it's joined to all four corners.

lines.text: The triangles on the bottom, right and top sides have areas fifteen, twenty-two and twenty-five.
lines.caption: The triangles on the bottom, right and top sides have areas fifteen, twenty-two and twenty-five.

lines.text: What is the area of the triangle on the left side?
lines.caption: What is the area of the triangle on the left side?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's break it down. P is joined to all four corners, so we get four triangles.
lines.caption: Let's break it down. P is joined to all four corners, so we get four triangles.

lines.text: Each triangle sits on one side of the rectangle.
lines.caption: Each triangle sits on one side of the rectangle.

lines.text: The bottom one has area fifteen, the right one has twenty-two, and the top one has twenty-five.
lines.caption: The bottom one has area fifteen, the right one has twenty-two, and the top one has twenty-five.

lines.text: We want the area of the left one.
lines.caption: We want the area of the left one.

lines.text: We don't know how big the rectangle is, or exactly where P is. That's the puzzle!
lines.caption: We don't know how big the rectangle is, or exactly where P is. That's the puzzle!

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's use the area rule: one over two, times base, times height.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's use the area rule: one over two, times base, times height.

lines.text: Look at the bottom triangle and the top triangle together.
lines.caption: Look at the bottom triangle and the top triangle together.

lines.text: The bottom side and the top side have the same length: the width of the rectangle.
lines.caption: The bottom side and the top side have the same length: the width of the rectangle.

lines.text: The bottom triangle's height goes from P down to the bottom side.
lines.caption: The bottom triangle's height goes from P down to the bottom side.

lines.text: The top triangle's height goes from P up to the top side.
lines.caption: The top triangle's height goes from P up to the top side.

lines.text: Stack those two heights, and they make the full height of the rectangle.
lines.caption: Stack those two heights, and they make the full height of the rectangle.

lines.text: Add the two areas, and you get the width times the full height, divided by two.
lines.caption: Add the two areas, and you get the width times the full height, divided by two.

lines.text: Width times height is the whole rectangle. So the pair makes HALF the rectangle!
lines.caption: Width times height is the whole rectangle. So the pair makes HALF the rectangle!

lines.text: Watch P slide up and down. One triangle grows, and the other one shrinks.
lines.caption: Watch P slide up and down. One triangle grows, and the other one shrinks.

lines.text: But their total never changes. It stays half the rectangle.
lines.caption: But their total never changes. It stays half the rectangle.

lines.text: The same idea works for the left and right triangles.
lines.caption: The same idea works for the left and right triangles.

lines.text: Their bases are the left and right sides, and their heights add up to the width.
lines.caption: Their bases are the left and right sides, and their heights add up to the width.

lines.text: So that pair makes the other half.
lines.caption: So that pair makes the other half.

lines.text: Bottom plus top is fifteen plus twenty-five, which is forty. That's half the rectangle.
lines.caption: Bottom plus top is fifteen plus twenty-five, which is forty. That's half the rectangle.

lines.text: So the right one plus the left one is also forty.
lines.caption: So the right one plus the left one is also forty.

lines.text: Twenty-two plus the left one is forty. <short pause> So the left one is eighteen. The answer is C!
lines.caption: Twenty-two plus the left one is forty. So the left one is eighteen. The answer is C!

lines.text: Let's double-check. Bottom plus top is forty, so the whole rectangle is two times forty: eighty.
lines.caption: Let's double-check. Bottom plus top is forty, so the whole rectangle is two times forty: eighty.

lines.text: Take away fifteen, twenty-two and twenty-five. That leaves eighteen. It matches!
lines.caption: Take away fifteen, twenty-two and twenty-five. That leaves eighteen. It matches!

lines.text: Here's a second way to SEE it, just by cutting.
lines.caption: Here's a second way to SEE it, just by cutting.

lines.text: Draw a line across through P, and a line up and down through P.
lines.caption: Draw a line across through P, and a line up and down through P.

lines.text: Now the big rectangle is made of four small rectangles.
lines.caption: Now the big rectangle is made of four small rectangles.

lines.text: The line from P to a corner cuts each small rectangle into two matching halves.
lines.caption: The line from P to a corner cuts each small rectangle into two matching halves.

lines.text: In every small rectangle, one piece belongs to the top or bottom triangle.
lines.caption: In every small rectangle, one piece belongs to the top or bottom triangle.

lines.text: The other piece belongs to the left or right triangle.
lines.caption: The other piece belongs to the left or right triangle.

lines.text: So top plus bottom gets exactly half of the whole rectangle, and left plus right gets the rest.
lines.caption: So top plus bottom gets exactly half of the whole rectangle, and left plus right gets the rest.

lines.text: When would you pick this one? When you want to see why the rule is true.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? When you want to see why the rule is true.

lines.text: Now let's look at the traps.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the traps.

lines.text: Twenty-two feels right, because it sits across from the missing triangle.
lines.caption: Twenty-two feels right, because it sits across from the missing triangle.

lines.text: But left and right only match when P is halfway across. Here, P is a bit to the left.
lines.caption: But left and right only match when P is halfway across. Here, P is a bit to the left.

lines.text: Twelve comes from pairing neighbours: fifteen plus twenty-two, take away twenty-five.
lines.caption: Twelve comes from pairing neighbours: fifteen plus twenty-two, take away twenty-five.

lines.text: But neighbours don't make a pair. Fifteen plus twenty-two is thirty-seven, not forty.
lines.caption: But neighbours don't make a pair. Fifteen plus twenty-two is thirty-seven, not forty.

lines.text: Fifteen just copies the bottom triangle. Nothing makes the left one match it.
lines.caption: Fifteen just copies the bottom triangle. Nothing makes the left one match it.

lines.text: Twenty-eight is too big. The left and right pair would be fifty, but each pair must be forty.
lines.caption: Twenty-eight is too big. The left and right pair would be fifty, but each pair must be forty.

lines.text: Quick check for any answer: opposite pairs must have the same total.
lines.caption: Quick check for any answer: opposite pairs must have the same total.

lines.text: Your turn! Same trick, new numbers.
lines.caption: Your turn! Same trick, new numbers.

lines.text: This time, the bottom triangle is nine, the right one is twenty, and the left one is sixteen.
lines.caption: This time, the bottom triangle is nine, the right one is twenty, and the left one is sixteen.

lines.text: Find the area of the top triangle. Bonus: find the area of the whole rectangle.
lines.caption: Find the area of the top triangle. Bonus: find the area of the whole rectangle.

lines.text: Pause the video and try it. Which pair do you know completely?
lines.caption: Pause the video and try it. Which pair do you know completely?

lines.text: Welcome back! This time, the pair we know is left and right.
lines.caption: Welcome back! This time, the pair we know is left and right.

lines.text: Sixteen plus twenty is thirty-six. That's half the rectangle.
lines.caption: Sixteen plus twenty is thirty-six. That's half the rectangle.

lines.text: So bottom plus top is also thirty-six.
lines.caption: So bottom plus top is also thirty-six.

lines.text: Nine plus the top one is thirty-six, so the top triangle is twenty-seven.
lines.caption: Nine plus the top one is thirty-six, so the top triangle is twenty-seven.

lines.text: And the whole rectangle is two times thirty-six, which is seventy-two.
lines.caption: And the whole rectangle is two times thirty-six, which is seventy-two.

lines.text: Amazing work if you got both!
lines.caption: Amazing work if you got both!

lines.text: Let's recap. Join a point inside a rectangle to all four corners.
lines.caption: Let's recap. Join a point inside a rectangle to all four corners.

lines.text: Opposite triangles always add up to half the rectangle, wherever the point is.
lines.caption: Opposite triangles always add up to half the rectangle, wherever the point is.
